Rashi on Gittin 28a:10:1.hebrew: אסורה לאכול - בת ישראל הנשואה לכהן שאוכלת בשבילו, אסורה מיד, דכל שעתא חיישינן עכשיו ימות, אלמא חיישינן למיתה:
Rashi on Gittin 28a:10:1.english: It is prohibited [for her] to eat - An Israelite woman who is married to a kohen, who eats [terumah] on his account, is prohibited immediately, for at every moment we are concerned [that] he will die now; thus, we are concerned about death:

Rashi on Gittin 28a:11:1.english: Teruma is possible - [for her] to be sustained on non-sacred produce:

Rashi on Gittin 28a:11:2.hebrew: גט לא אפשר - למיחש למיתה, דאי חיישת אין לך שולח גט לאשתו, והן עגונות:
Rashi on Gittin 28a:11:2.english: [For] a bill of divorce, it is not possible - to be concerned for [the husband's] death, for if you were concerned [about that], you would have no one sending a bill of divorce to his wife, and they would [remain] agunot [chained women]:

Rashi on Gittin 28a:14:1.hebrew: שאני התם שהרי אסרה שעה אחת קודם למיתתו - לעולם לא חיישינן למיתה, ושאני הכא שהרי אסרה מחיים שעה אחת קודם מיתתו, וכל שעתא איכא לספוקי בההיא שעתא שעתידה ליאסר. ושינויא דחיקא הוא, והיינו דפריך ליה: ואי לאו דחיישינן למיתה, ממאי דהוי גיטא דלעולם הוא מיית ברישא ונאסרה מחיים? דלמא היא מייתא ברישא, ולא יבא לכלל גט לעולם:
Rashi on Gittin 28a:14:1.english: It is different there, as he rendered her forbidden one hour prior to his death - In general, we are not concerned for death, but here it is different, as he rendered her forbidden [to eat terumah] during [his] lifetime, one hour prior to his death, and at every moment there is [reason] to be in doubt [that this is] that hour in which she is destined to become forbidden. And this is a forced answer, and that is why [Rav Pappa] objects to him: If we are not concerned for death, from where [is it known] that it will be a [valid] bill of divorce, [meaning] that he will certainly die first and she will become forbidden during [his] lifetime? Perhaps she will die first, and it will never take effect as a bill of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 28a:15:1.hebrew: אלא אמר אביי - האי תנא ודאי חייש למיתה, ולא קשיא: מתניתין דהכא ר' מאיר היא, דלא חייש לבקיעת הנוד:
Rashi on Gittin 28a:15:1.english: Rather, Abaye said - This Tanna [of the baraita] is certainly concerned about death, and there is no difficulty: our Mishnah here is [the opinion of] Rabbi Meir, who is not concerned about the bursting of the wineskin:

Rashi on Gittin 28a:17:1.english: [They] prohibit - lest the wineskin burst:

Rashi on Gittin 28a:1:1.english: Among his utensils - In his house:

Rashi on Gittin 28a:3:1.hebrew: לימא - רב יהודה: הלכה כיש אומרים, ולימא רבה: הלכה כר"ש; למה חזרו להזכיר את הדברים ולפרשן:
Rashi on Gittin 28a:3:1.english: Let [this sage] say - [i.e., let] Rav Yehuda [say]: the halakha is in accordance with "some say," and let Rabbah [say]: the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon [ben Elazar]; why did they go back to mention the [actual] statements and spell them out?

Rashi on Gittin 28a:3:2.hebrew: ומשני משום דאפכי להו - אית תנאי דמפכי דרבי שמעון ליש אומרים, ויש אומרים לרבי שמעון; הלכך אם לא הזכירו אלא שם החכמים, לא הוי ידעי אהייא מתרי לישני קיימי:
Rashi on Gittin 28a:3:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Because they reverse them - There are tannaim [reciters of traditions] who reverse [the opinion of] Rabbi Shimon [ben Elazar] to "Some say" and [that of] "Some say" to Rabbi Shimon; therefore, if they had mentioned only the names of the Sages, [people] would not know which of the two versions they are referring to:

Rashi on Gittin 28a:4:1.hebrew: חמת - בולזול"א בלע"ז, והיא של עור:
Rashi on Gittin 28a:4:1.english: A flask - Bolzele in Old French [a small leather pouch], and it is [made] of leather:

Rashi on Gittin 28a:4:2.english: Telika - tasche in Old French [a pouch or bag].

Rashi on Gittin 28a:5:1.hebrew: נותנו לה בחזקת שהוא קיים - ולא חיישינן שמא מת ובטל שליחותו, ומדאורייתא נפקא לן בהכל שוחטין (חולין דף י:), "העמד דבר על חזקתו":
Rashi on Gittin 28a:5:1.english: He gives it to her based on the presumption that he is alive - And we are not concerned that perhaps he died and [thereby] nullified his agency. And by Torah law, we derive [this principle] in [the chapter] Hakol Shochatin (Chullin 10b): "Maintain a thing in its presumptive status."

Rashi on Gittin 28a:6:1.hebrew: מקריבין אותה - ולא חיישינן שמא מתו בעליה, ולמיתה אזלא:
Rashi on Gittin 28a:6:1.english: They offer it - And we do not suspect that perhaps its owner died, and [therefore] it must be left to die:

Rashi on Gittin 28a:7:1.hebrew: לגבורות - שמונים שנה, לישנא דקרא (תהילים צ׳:י׳):
Rashi on Gittin 28a:7:1.english: [His years of] strength - Eighty years [of age]; [this is] the language of the verse (Psalms 90:10):

Rashi on Gittin 28a:7:2.hebrew: וחולה - או חולה דמתני', דוקא חולה ולא גוסס:
Rashi on Gittin 28a:7:2.english: And a sick person - [The phrase] "or a sick person" in the Mishnah [refers] specifically [to] a sick person, and not a moribund person:

Rashi on Gittin 28a:9:1.hebrew: כיון דאיפליג - משאר דרך כל הארץ, שהאריך ימים עד מאה שנה:
Rashi on Gittin 28a:9:1.english: Since he is set apart - from the rest of the way of all the world, in that he has lived long, to a hundred years:

Rashi on Gittin 28a:9:2.hebrew: איפליג - ואינו כשאר האדם להיות קרוב למות, אבל בן שמונים ואחת או יותר עד תשעים קרוב למות הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 28a:9:2.english: He is set apart - and he is not like other people [with respect to] being close to death; however, one who is eighty-one or more, up to ninety, is close to death.

Tosafot on Gittin 28a:11:1.hebrew: תרומה אפשר - תימה: וכי לא היה יודע המתרץ מתניתין דתרומה, ואיכא לאקשויי תרומה אתרומה כדבסמוך? וי"ל, דכן דרך הש"ס, שאינו חושש אלא מתרץ קושיא שמקשה לו:
Tosafot on Gittin 28a:11:1.english: Teruma is possible - It is astonishing: did the one who answered not know the Mishnah regarding teruma, [so] that one can raise a contradiction between teruma and teruma, as [the Gemara does] immediately below? And one can say that such is the way of the Talmud, that it is not concerned [with other difficulties], but rather answers the difficulty that is raised against it:

Tosafot on Gittin 28a:14:1.hebrew: שאני התם שהרי אסרה עליו שעה אחת מחיים - פירוש: הלך בעלה למדינת הים — אוכלת בתרומה, דהעמד בעלה בחזקת חי; אבל הכא, אפילו נעמידנו בחזקת חי, אסרה מחיים. ופריך: דלמא איהי מייתא ברישא, ולא תאסר מחיים:
Tosafot on Gittin 28a:14:1.english: It is different there, as he rendered her forbidden to himself one hour during [his] lifetime - Meaning: [Where] her husband went overseas, she eats teruma, because [we say] establish her husband in his presumptive status of being alive; but here, even if we establish him in his presumptive status of being alive, he has rendered her forbidden [during his] lifetime. And [Rav Pappa] objects: Perhaps she will die first, and she will not become forbidden during [his] lifetime:

Tosafot on Gittin 28a:15:1.hebrew: הא רבי מאיר דלא חייש למיתה כו' - השתא דמדמה שמא מת לשמא ימות, לא לגמרי מדמה. דהא ר' מאיר, דמוקי מתניתין כותיה ולא חייש לשמא מת אפילו לזמן מרובה, חייש לשמא ימות לזמן מרובה, דתנן בפרק ד' אחין (יבמות דף כו.): ארבעה אחין, שנים מהן נשואין שתי אחיות, ומתו הנשואים את האחיות — הרי אלו חולצות ולא מתיבמות. ומפרש בגמ': משום דקסבר אסור לבטל מצות יבמין, ודלמא אדמייבם חד מיית אידך, וקא מבטל מצות יבמין. וההיא משנה מוקי לה כר"מ בפ"ב דיבמות (דף יח.). ולקמן בפרק בתרא (גיטין דף פה.) נמי אמר: לכולי עלמא גירות לא שכיחא, מיתה שכיחא. ולרבי יהודה נמי, דחייש לשמא ימות לאלתר, לא חייש לשמא מת לאלתר; דאם לא כן, אשת כהן שיצא בעלה מפתח ביתו לא תאכל בתרומה, ולא תאכל כי אם בשעה שרואה בעלה בפניה! אלא ודאי לא מדמה אלא שמא מת לזמן מרובה לשמא ימות לאלתר:
Tosafot on Gittin 28a:15:1.english: This [is] Rabbi Meir, who is not concerned about death, etc. - Now that [Abaye] compares [the concern that] perhaps he died to [the concern that] perhaps he will die, he does not compare [them] completely. For Rabbi Meir, in accordance with whom [Abaye] establishes our Mishnah and who is not concerned that perhaps he died even over a long period, is [nevertheless] concerned that perhaps he will die over a long period; as we learned in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achin (Yevamot 26a): "[If there were] four brothers, two of whom were married to two sisters, and those married to the sisters died, behold, these [widows] perform chalitzah and may not enter into levirate marriage." And it is explained in the Gemara: because [the Tanna] holds it is forbidden to nullify the mitzvah of yevamin [the surviving brothers], and perhaps while one performs levirate marriage the other will die, and he will nullify the mitzvah of yevamin. And that Mishnah [the Gemara] establishes in accordance with Rabbi Meir in the second chapter of Yevamot (18a). And later in the last chapter [of this tractate] (Gittin 85a) it also says: According to everyone, divorce is uncommon, [whereas] death is common. And according to Rabbi Yehuda as well, who is concerned that perhaps he will die immediately, he is not concerned that perhaps he [already] died immediately; for if not so, the wife of a kohen whose husband went out from the doorway of his house would not eat terumah, and would only eat [it] when she sees her husband before her! Rather, certainly [Abaye] only compares [the concern that] perhaps he died over a long period to [the concern that] perhaps he will die immediately:

Tosafot on Gittin 28a:1:1.hebrew: או שמצאו בין כליו - פי': בביתו; אע"ג דרבים מצויין בביתו, ואם היא נמצאת בקרקע היה לחוש ליוסף בן שמעון אחר, אבל בין כליו ליכא למיחש שמא הביאו אחר, אלא הוא:
Tosafot on Gittin 28a:1:1.english: Or where he found it among his utensils - Meaning: in his house. Even though many [people] frequent his house, and if it were found on the ground there would be [reason] to suspect another Yosef ben Shimon, [nevertheless] among his utensils there is no [reason] to suspect that another [person] brought it, rather [it was] he:

Tosafot on Gittin 28a:4:1.hebrew: מצאו בחפיסה או בדלוסקמא ומכירו כשר - כשמצאו הוא עצמו איירי, מדסמכינן אהכרתו. ואע"ג דלאו צורבא מדרבנן הוא, נאמן במיגו דאי בעי אמר "לא אבדתי", דכולי עלמא אית להו טביעות עינא, כדפירשנו לעיל. ו"מכירו" אחפיסה ואדלוסקמא קאי, ואע"פ שאינו מכיר את הגט; דאי מכיר את הגט, למה לי שמצאו בחפיסה? וא"ת: וניחוש לשאלה, כדאמרינן בפרק בתרא דיבמות (דף קכ:)? וי"ל: דקים ליה בנפשיה שלא השאילה לשום אדם. אי נמי, ביודע שבחפיסה או בדלוסקמא איבדו, ומכל מקום צריך שיהא מכיר חפיסה או דלוסקמא בטביעות עינא, דמה שיודע שבחפיסה או בדלוסקמא איבדו אין זה סימן. והא דתנן בפ"ק דב"מ (דף כ.): "מצא בחפיסה או בדלוסקמא תכריך של שטרות או אגודה של שטרות כו'" — התם מיירי שנותן סימן בחפיסה או בדלוסקמא עצמו, ועל ידו מחזיר לו מה שבתוכו, ולא חיישינן לשאלה לענין ממון. אבל מה שאומר שאבדה בדלוסקמא לא הוי סימן, דדרך להניח שטרות בדלוסקמא, כדתניא בתוספתא: "עשר דלוסקמאות שטרות מסרתי לך"; ואפילו הוי סימן, סימן מובהק להחזיר הגט לא הוי. והא דאמר באלו מציאות (ב"מ דף כח.): "הוא אומר בחפיסה והיא אומרת בחפיסה, ינתן לו, דמידע ידעה דכל דאית ליה בחפיסה מנח ליה" — אפילו תימצי לומר ד"ינתן לו לגרש בו" קאמר, לא משום דחשיב סימן מובהק, דהתם מיירי בשלא הוחזק יוסף בן שמעון אחר, ואותו הגט ודאי נכתב לשמו, אלא שאין ידוע אם נפל מן הבעל או מן האשה. אי נמי: "ומכירו" פירוש "או מכירו", ויש ספרים דגרסי בהדיא "או מכירו", והכי פירושו: מצאו בחפיסה או בדלוסקמא וידוע שהוא שלו וגם שבתוכה איבדו, אע"פ שאינו מכיר הגט, או מכירו — שמכיר הגט אפילו בלא חפיסה. ויש ספרים דגרסי "אם מכירו", הכי פירושו: מצאו בחפיסה ויודע שלא בתוכה איבדו ואינו שלו, ואפילו הכי אם מכירו כשר, ולרבותא נקט "מצאו בחפיסה". אי נמי: דווקא אם מכירו כשר, אבל מה שהוא יודע שבחפיסה או בדלוסקמא איבדו אינו מועיל; ולספרים דגרסי "ומכירו" מצי לפרש כמו "אם מכירו":
Tosafot on Gittin 28a:4:1.english: If he found it in a ḥafisa or in a deluskema and recognizes it, it is valid - It speaks of when he himself found it, since we rely on his recognition. And even though he is not a rabbinic scholar, he is believed through a migo [argument, i.e.,] that if he wanted he could have said, "I did not lose [it]," for everyone has visual recognition [of their own items], as we explained above. And "recognizes it" refers to the ḥafisa and to the deluskema, even though he does not recognize the get; for if he recognizes the get, why do I need that he found it in a ḥafisa? And if you say: Let us be concerned about borrowing [i.e., that someone else borrowed the container and lost the get inside it], as we say in the last chapter of Yevamot (120b)? One can answer: He is certain in himself that he did not lend it to any person. Alternatively, [it is] where he knows that he lost it in a ḥafisa or in a deluskema, and nevertheless he must recognize the ḥafisa or deluskema by visual recognition, for the fact that he knows he lost it in a ḥafisa or deluskema is not a [valid] sign. And as for that which we learned in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (20a): "If one found in a ḥafisa or in a deluskema a bundle of documents or a packet of documents, etc." — there it is speaking of where he gives a [distinguishing] sign on the ḥafisa or deluskema itself, and through it [the finder] returns to him what is inside it, and we are not concerned about borrowing regarding monetary matters. However, the fact that he says he lost it in a deluskema is not a [valid] sign, for it is usual to place documents in a deluskema, as it is taught in the Tosefta: "Ten deluskemaot of documents I handed over to you"; and even if it were a sign, it is not a definitive sign [by which] to return a get. And as for that which it says in [the chapter] Elu Metziot (Bava Metzia 28a): "He says [it was] in a ḥafisa and she says [it was] in a ḥafisa, it should be given to him, for she certainly knows that everything he has he places in a ḥafisa" — even if you conclude and say that it means "it should be given to him to divorce with it," [that is] not because it is considered a definitive sign, for there it is speaking of where no other Yosef ben Shimon was established [to be in the city], and that get was certainly written for him, only it is not known whether it fell from the husband or from the wife. Alternatively: "and recognizes it" means "or recognizes it," and there are texts that explicitly read "or recognizes it," and this is its explanation: [If] he found it in a ḥafisa or in a deluskema and it is known that it is his and also that he lost it inside it, even though he does not recognize the get; or he recognizes it — meaning he recognizes the get even without a ḥafisa. And there are texts that read "if he recognizes it"; this is its explanation: He found it in a ḥafisa and knows that he did not lose it inside it and it is not his, and even so, if he recognizes it, it is valid, and it stated "found it in a ḥafisa" for novelty. Alternatively: specifically if he recognizes it, it is valid, whereas the fact that he knows he lost it in a ḥafisa or in a deluskema is of no avail; and according to the texts that read "and recognizes it," one can explain it like "if he recognizes it":

Tosafot on Gittin 28a:5:1.hebrew: והניחו זקן או חולה כו' - תימה, דבפרק המפקיד (ב"מ דף לט:) גבי ההיא סבתא דאישתבאי איהי וחדא ברתא, אמרינן: דלמא שכיבא סבתא, דלמא שכיבא ברתא. ואומר ר"י: דלענין יתמי החמירו טפי למיחש, כדקאמר נמי התם: לא שנא עבוד עיטרא, לא שנא לא עבוד — חיישינן; ובחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף כט:) מפלגינן בין עבוד עיטרא ללא עבוד, דאמר: עיטרא קלא איתלה. ועוד, דבשבויות חיישינן טפי למיתה:
Tosafot on Gittin 28a:5:1.english: And he left him elderly or sick, etc. - It is astonishing, for in the chapter [entitled] HaMafkid (Bava Metzia 39b), regarding that grandmother who was taken captive — she and one daughter — we say: "Perhaps the grandmother died, perhaps the daughter died" [and we do not presume she is alive]! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that with respect to orphans, [the Sages] were stricter to be concerned [about death], just as [the Gemara] also says there: Whether they drew up a written agreement (itra) or did not draw up [one], we are concerned; whereas in [the chapter entitled] Chezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 29b), we distinguish between where they drew up a written agreement and where they did not, for [the Gemara] says: A written agreement generates publicity. And furthermore, regarding captive women, we are more concerned about death:
